headline: A bill asking US states to consider making large data centers pay for their grid upgrades failed to advance in the Senate, short of the 60 votes needed.
score_reason: Stays at the pool score: a real Senate vote on who pays for AI's power demand, though the account comes from an industry-group column.
importance_line: Households and small businesses that pay electricity bills are the people the bill is meant to protect, but the account rests on an industry-group column, and it does not say whether a new vote is planned.
summary: In an opinion column for CoinDesk, relayed by The Cryptonomist, Rashan Colbert, director of US policy at the Crypto Council for Innovation, an industry group, writes about a Senate procedural vote in which the Ratepayer Protection Act drew 57 votes for and 43 against, short of the 60 needed, after passing the House 417 to 3. The bill would make state regulators and some utilities consider requiring data centers of 100 megawatts or more to cover the full extra cost of power generation and grid upgrades built for them, leaving the decision to each state.
notes: Facts come from an opinion column by an industry-group official, relayed by Cryptonomist (AI-assisted article); vote date not stated.
